When you visit the INDAPT website at indapt.net, send us an enquiry or discuss a project, that interaction involves information about you and your work. This Privacy Policy sets out the principles governing the use of that information, explains cookies and describes how to exercise your rights.

In this Policy, INDAPT refers to the team and participants working under the shared brand in relation to the particular interaction. Different service providers may be involved according to the task, country and region. Access to information depends on their role and need, rather than merely sharing a brand. The participant that actually determines the purposes and means of processing is responsible for those decisions under applicable law.
Situations covered by this Policy

This Policy concerns the public website, initial enquiries, business correspondence and related interactions with clients, prospective clients, organisation representatives, partners and specialists. Separate sections explain collaboration proposals, CVs and complaints.

Where a particular product, event, recruitment exercise or project requires an additional notice, it is provided for that situation. The website Policy does not replace processing terms for a client's product, employment documentation or a project data processing agreement.

These rules concern personal data: information relating to a directly or indirectly identifiable individual. A work email, business telephone number and company representative's name may also be personal data. Information about an organisation that is not linked to an identifiable individual is not, by itself, personal data.
Information that may be processed

An enquiry may include your name, email, telephone number, organisation, role, preferred contact method, task description and attachments. Subsequent discussions may add correspondence, agreed actions and working comments needed to respond.

During a visit, technical systems receive information needed to deliver pages and provide protection: IP address, request time, page address, browser type, device information and error messages. Permitted analytics may involve browser identifiers, referral sources and page interactions.

Separate records may evidence consent and withdrawal, selected preferences, delivery of a required notice and completion of a data request. They are used to confirm those actions rather than expand the original purpose of an enquiry.
Sources of information

You are the main source, through a form, email, message, brief or another agreed channel. Technical information arises from the browser and systems supporting the website. A particular external service's notice may explain additional aspects of its operation.

A business contact may come from your colleague, client, organisation representative or partner. There must be a lawful basis for sharing and using it. A business card, public profile or published work address is not permission for unrestricted use or advertising mailings.

Where information is not obtained from you, details about the source, purpose, data categories and party responsible for processing are provided in the circumstances and within the periods required by applicable law. A shared team does not remove this duty.
When you browse the website

Technical information is used to deliver the requested page, support compatibility, identify errors and protect against abuse. Necessary processing is limited to those tasks. Reading public pages does not require you to submit a brief or provide your name and telephone number.

Permitted analytics helps identify useful materials and website elements needing improvement. Analytics conditions and choices are explained below. Viewing a page does not constitute consent to advertising messages, public disclosure of personal data or sharing all information with any partner.
When you send an enquiry or brief

Contact details, task descriptions and necessary attachments are used to respond, clarify the request, assess possible involvement and prepare a proposal. Specialists may participate where they need access to the relevant information. The need to involve another participant is assessed before data is shared with them.

An initial enquiry does not require an entire client dataset or access to your infrastructure. If further information is needed for assessment, we explain its purpose and agree a transfer method. Do not include material unnecessary for reviewing the brief.

Moving from an enquiry to a project does not automatically authorise all subsequent data operations. The participants, purposes, access, retention and necessary processing documents are determined for contractual delivery.
Business correspondence and professional contacts

Correspondence involves your address, name, message content, attachments and technical delivery information. These allow a substantive response, a record of arrangements and continuation of the agreed discussion. An organisation representative's contact is used in connection with their professional role.

If you tell us that you no longer handle a matter or represent a different organisation, the relevant contact information is updated. Initial communication does not require a passport, home address or other information unrelated to the task.

Email, messaging and video meeting providers have their own terms for technical data processing. Where content needs greater protection, the communication channel is agreed in advance. Recording a call or meeting requires advance notice and an appropriate basis; a meeting invitation does not, by itself, permit recording and publication.
Proposals from partners and specialists

If you offer services, a partnership or project involvement, information about your professional experience, skills and contacts is used to assess the proposal and discuss terms. It does not become public or available to every INDAPT participant merely because it may be professionally relevant.

Sharing your CV, profile or contact information with a client requires its own basis and a clear purpose. Permission to consider an initial proposal is not indefinite permission to recommend you to any third party.
When you submit a CV

Your CV, portfolio, contacts and correspondence relevant to a proposed role are used to consider that collaboration opportunity. Initial assessment does not require health information, political views, family circumstances or documents for formal employment or other relationships.

Assessment for one role does not imply indefinite inclusion in a talent pool. Keeping a profile for future opportunities, requesting references and sending a CV to another independent company require a separate lawful basis and any necessary notice.
If discussions progress to a specific offer, the relationship terms and processing of the documents needed for it are addressed separately.
Subscriptions and advertising messages

A response to your question, clarification of a brief and working messages about an agreed project are distinct from advertising mailings. A website enquiry, exchange of business cards or participation in negotiations does not automatically subscribe you to advertising.

Where a news or advertising subscription is offered, the relevant consent is requested separately where required. Selected topics and communication channels must not be expanded arbitrarily. Declining a mailing does not prevent an enquiry or consideration of a business proposal.

Use the opt-out method in a message or email hello@indapt.net. Advertising processing stops immediately on request. A minimal opt-out record may be kept to avoid adding you to the same mailing again without a basis. Necessary communications under an existing contract are considered separately from advertising.
Complaints and data requests

If you report a breach, inaccuracy or problem, information needed to investigate, respond and fulfil a lawful request is used. It may include contacts, the circumstances, relevant correspondence and evidence of a representative's authority.

Access during a review is limited to those who need to investigate. If part of a complaint must be shared with another participant to respond, disclosure is limited to what is necessary. We consider requests for confidentiality but cannot promise anonymous investigation where material circumstances must be disclosed for the review or the law requires otherwise.
Rights procedures and response periods are explained below. Making a complaint is not a basis for using its content in advertising, public case studies or unrelated projects.
Lawful grounds for using information

Where processing relies on consent, that consent must be specific, informed and capable of being evidenced. Consent to handling an enquiry is obtained separately from confirmation of other documents. Reading this Policy, closing a window or visiting the website does not replace consent.

If you personally are a prospective contracting party, necessary information may be used to take steps at your request before a contract and to perform it. Communications with an organisation's representative, website protection and business enquiries may rely on legitimate interests where the law allows and individual rights are not infringed. The relevant interest is responding to a business request, safeguarding systems or protecting a particular right, rather than unrestricted use of contacts.

Some records are needed to meet statutory duties, comply with court orders and protect rights in a dispute. A change of purpose requires assessment of the new basis and any additional notice or consent. Withdrawn consent must not be arbitrarily replaced with another basis to continue the same optional processing.
If you choose not to provide information

You decide what optional information to provide. If a contact is needed to respond or a task description is needed to assess a proposal, its absence limits consideration of the enquiry rather than your right to read public website pages.

Any statutory or contractual requirement to provide particular data, and the consequences of not providing it, must be explained beforehand. Optional analytics, advertising and testimonial publication must not become conditions of an ordinary enquiry where there is no objective need for them.
Cookies and similar technologies

Cookies are small records a browser stores when working with a website. Local storage, pixels and request identifiers can perform similar functions. They help maintain a session, remember choices and produce statistics. An identifier without a name is not necessarily anonymous.

Functions fall into necessary technologies, additional convenience preferences, analytics and advertising tools. Necessity is assessed by function: a technology useful to a website owner for marketing does not become necessary to deliver a requested page merely because it has a technical label.

Necessary functions are limited to operating the requested service, security and retaining user choices to the extent needed. Additional functions take account of your choices and applicable requirements. This Policy provides for prior consent to optional analytics.
Yandex Metrica analytics

Yandex Metrica is used for statistics on the Russian version of the INDAPT website. Google Analytics is not used on that version. Metrica processes technical and interaction information within the permitted settings and user choices. Names, emails, telephone numbers, enquiry text and attachments must not be sent as analytics parameters or included in page addresses.

The provider documents some longer-lived cookies: for example, _ym_uid lasts one year and _ym_isad lasts 20 hours. These illustrate the provider's standard periods and do not assert that every such file is installed on every visit to the INDAPT website. The actual set depends on enabled functions and browser settings.

The provider's technology and expiry information is at https://yandex.ru/support/metrica/en/general/cookie-usage, and its privacy policy is at https://yandex.ru/legal/confidential/. A cookie's lifetime on a device and retention of a record in a report are different matters.

Session recording, advertising retargeting, contact matching and combination with external advertising datasets are not covered by general permission for website operation. Enabling them requires the appropriate information, settings and a separate lawful basis. Mentioning a technology in a case study does not mean its tracker runs on the website.
Google Analytics on international sections

Google Analytics 4 may be used on international sections of the INDAPT website. Its use concerns the pages and functions where it is actually enabled, subject to necessary restrictions and user choices. Mentioning Google Analytics in this Policy does not mean that it is used on every website page.

Where enabled, the service is used to assess visits, referral sources and interactions with materials. Processing may involve browser identifiers, session, page and event information, device details and approximate location. Names, emails, telephone numbers and enquiry content must not be sent to Google Analytics through page addresses, event names or analytics parameters.

Cookies named _ga and _ga_ with a container identifier may be used to distinguish visits. Google's documentation gives a default expiry of two years; website settings and browser restrictions may change the actual period. Cookie expiry is not the retention period for all analytics information: user and event records have separate retention settings, limited by the processing purpose.

Google's processing information is at https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites, cookie information at https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/11397207 and retention settings at https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/7667196. Any necessary transfer to the provider follows the International interactions section, including required grounds and safeguards; selecting English does not, by itself, authorise that transfer.

Prior consent remains the rule for optional analytics. The absence of cookies does not necessarily mean that no information is transmitted: some Google modes allow measurements to be sent without cookies. Under this Policy, optional analytics measurements must not be transmitted before consent or following refusal, including through such requests. Advertising personalisation, Google Ads, remarketing and matching with other data require their own settings, notices and lawful basis.

You may decline or withdraw consent through the INDAPT website's cookie controls and the general privacy contact. Google's additional tool for supported browsers is available at https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout. It does not replace website choice controls or automatically erase information already received.
Managing cookies and external elements

Optional categories are selected separately from necessary ones. Service information must reflect actual deployment: where more than one analytics provider receives information, each provider's involvement is disclosed regardless of the page language. Declining, accepting and changing choices must be clear; inaction, scrolling and continued browsing are not consent. Declining analytics must not prevent reading the main pages or sending an ordinary enquiry.

You can change choices through the cookie controls available on the website. You may also restrict or delete cookies through your browser. Deleting the preference record may cause the website to request a choice again. Choices may differ between devices and browsers.

If a relevant control is unavailable or does not work, email hello@indapt.net; related requests to stop processing follow the applicable procedure. An email does not itself remove files from your browser, and deleting files does not automatically erase information already received by other systems.

An external video, map, widget or social platform button may contact its provider's servers when loaded. Required notices and user choices are considered before an optional transfer. Following an external link and loading an embedded element have different data sharing consequences.
Who may receive access

Where necessary, access may be provided to specialists considering an enquiry; providers delivering agreed work; hosting, communications, email, enquiry management and technical support providers; and professional advisers handling a relevant matter. Each category is used only where there is an actual need and an appropriate basis.

A processor receives a defined task, permitted operations and confidentiality and security requirements. An independent recipient is responsible for its own purposes and necessary notices. These roles must not be confused: arrangements between participants do not remove duties to the individual.

The shared INDAPT name, membership of a partner ecosystem or a website logo does not automatically grant access to enquiries. We do not sell enquiry data or provide it to other companies for their independent advertising mailings. Information may be provided to a court, regulator or other authority within the scope of a lawful requirement.
International interactions

Working across countries does not permit unrestricted movement of all data between any participants. Before a necessary international transfer, its purpose, recipient, information, basis and required safeguards are established. Required notifications and regulatory restrictions must be observed.

Applicable requirements to use databases in the Russian Federation when collecting Russian citizens' data and carrying out related operations remain effective. A foreign website language or overseas project participant does not remove those requirements. Any subsequent international transfer is assessed separately.

Where GDPR, UK GDPR or another foreign regime applies to particular processing, its mandatory requirements also apply, including the relevant transfer mechanism and necessary information about recipients and protection. A list of countries of operation does not describe the actual data route. Information about a transfer and its safeguards may be requested through the general privacy contact.
Client information in project delivery

Where a client instructs processing of its product users' data, INDAPT's actions are defined by the project agreement and the authorised party's instructions. That product's data does not become a general INDAPT contact database and must not be used for our own mailings or other projects without a separate basis.

A request about data in a client system may require the involvement of the client as the party determining the purposes of processing. The request is then directed appropriately while preserving confidentiality. This does not remove the receiving participant's own duties.
Automation and sensitive information

Technical filters may help detect spam, errors and threats. Analytics statistics do not themselves mean that a decision with legal effects is being made about an individual. Such solely automated processing is outside ordinary enquiry handling; introducing it would require its own basis, explanation and statutory safeguards.

Sending enquiry content, CVs or client materials to an external artificial intelligence tool is also a data operation. It requires assessment of the provider's terms, purpose, access and lawful basis. Simply submitting a brief does not permit uploading it to a public service for independent model training or disclosure to other users.

General forms are not intended for special category data, identification biometrics, health information, identity documents or payment card details. If received unnecessarily, use is restricted to assessing lawfulness and arranging deletion or return, subject to mandatory requirements.
How retention is determined

Retention depends on the purpose, information involved, development of the relationship and mandatory requirements. Data must not be kept indefinitely merely because it once arrived through the website. When a purpose ends, any further need and basis for retention are assessed.

Enquiries and briefs are needed until consideration and agreed further discussions are complete. If a project begins, necessary records follow the relevant contractual process. A specialist's proposal or CV is used for the role under consideration; separate retention for future opportunities needs its own basis.

Complaint records are retained for resolution and necessary legal protection. Contractual, accounting and other mandatory documents follow applicable statutory periods. Evidence of consent and refusal is limited to what is needed to demonstrate choices and fulfil duties; this does not justify retaining all enquiry attachments.

Technical records are used for diagnosis and security for the necessary period. A record relevant to an incident may be isolated for investigation. Analytics retention takes account of the purpose, settings and limits of the relevant service. Ask hello@indapt.net for the applicable period or criteria for your information.
Protection and ending processing

Access is restricted by task and authority, with organisational and technical safeguards appropriate to the risk. Requirements also extend to appointed processors. An incident triggers containment measures and applicable statutory notification duties.
No internet resource can promise absolute technical security. This does not remove responsibility for meeting security requirements or allow all consequences of a breach to be placed on the visitor.

When a basis ends and no other lawful basis remains, processing ends and data is destroyed within the required periods. Where mandatory retention is necessary, access and use are limited to that purpose. Deletion must cover operational systems and appointed processors; backups are not used to restart ended processing and are cleared under legally permitted arrangements.
Your rights

You may request processing information and access to your data, correction of inaccuracies, restriction or destruction of unlawfully obtained or excessive information, withdrawal of consent and cessation of processing in the circumstances provided by law.

Where relevant provisions apply, rights also include restriction, objection, portability and safeguards for solely automated decisions. The available rights and conditions for exercising them depend on the particular processing and applicable law.

You may object to direct marketing at any time. Withdrawing consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing before withdrawal. It may end an aspect of the relationship for which the information is objectively necessary, but does not justify a penalty or arbitrary reduction in access to public materials.
Making a request and receiving a response

Email hello@indapt.net with the subject Personal data. Explain what you want done, the contact you used and the relevant interaction. Where needed, we proportionately verify identity or representative authority to avoid disclosure to someone else. Do not send a passport copy in an initial ordinary email.

Under Russian rules, information and access requests are normally handled within 10 working days; a legally permitted, reasoned extension is no longer than five working days. A request to cease processing follows the statutory period of up to 10 working days, with a permissible reasoned extension of up to five working days and statutory exceptions.

In relevant cases where a purpose ends or consent is withdrawn, data is destroyed within 30 days unless another lawful basis or applicable exception remains. Confirmed inaccuracies and identified unlawful processing have separate, shorter statutory deadlines. Where GDPR or UK GDPR applies, its response periods and permitted extensions are observed. Any applicable shorter mandatory deadline remains effective.

If a request cannot be met in full, we explain the basis and available actions. Other people's rights, mandatory retention and lawful exceptions are assessed for the particular request; administrative convenience alone is not sufficient grounds for refusal.
Complaints to authorities
You may contact hello@indapt.net about processing. You may also approach Roskomnadzor through its official website, https://rkn.gov.ru, a competent court or another authorised body.

Where the UK regime applies, complaints information is available from the Information Commissioner's Office at https://ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint/. Where GDPR applies, you retain the right to approach the competent supervisory authority in the relevant country. Correspondence with INDAPT is not a prerequisite to exercising those rights.
Children and external resources

The website is intended for a professional business audience and is not designed to collect children's data. If a child's information is received without a necessary basis, processing is restricted to checking the circumstances and arranging cessation or deletion under the applicable procedure.

This Policy does not govern external website owners' independent actions after you follow their links. Their forms, accounts and services have their own notices. Retention of links or copies following online publication may be outside INDAPT's control; this should be considered before agreeing to public disclosure.
Policy updates

We update this Policy as the website, interactions and applicable requirements develop. The month and year of the latest update appear above. The Russian and English versions describe the same principles and situations.

A revision does not automatically expand previous consent or make past processing without a basis lawful. A material change in purpose or use requires the relevant notice and fresh consent where necessary.
For all privacy enquiries: hello@indapt.net.
